common_names: Brazilian rosewood; Rio rosewood; Bahia rosewood; jacarandá-da-bahia; palissandre de Rio
deposits: dark red-brown gum in some pores
heartwood: Dark chocolate-brown to purplish/reddish brown with irregular black streaks (spider-web figure); oily feel.
odour: Distinct sweet, rose-like scent when freshly cut.
key_diagnostic: Dark heartwood with black streaks + rose scent + medium pores (few, solitary/short multiples) + banded/aliform parenchyma + very fine rays. Cannot be separated reliably from other Dalbergia (esp. D. spruceana, D. latifolia) by hand lens alone.
lookalikes: Dalbergia spruceana (Amazon rosewood); Dalbergia latifolia (Indian rosewood); Machaerium scleroxylon (Santos rosewood / pau ferro); Dalbergia baronii / D. maritima (Madagascar)

common_names: Guatemalan fir; pinabete
heartwood: Creamy white to pale buff; no distinct heartwood colour.
odour: Faint, sometimes unpleasant when green; non-resinous.
key_diagnostic: Pale, non-resinous softwood with NO resin canals and no colour difference between heartwood and sapwood. Typical 'fir' - genus level only. Mostly traded as Christmas trees/branches rather than timber.
lookalikes: Other Abies spp.; Picea spp. (spruce - but spruce HAS small resin canals); Tsuga spp.

common_names: Monkey puzzle; Chilean pine; pehuén; araucaria
heartwood: Pale yellowish to light brown, sometimes with a pinkish tinge.
key_diagnostic: Uniform, fine-textured softwood with faint growth rings and no resin canals. Separation from other Araucaria (e.g. Paraná pine A. angustifolia) needs microscopy or DNA.
lookalikes: Araucaria angustifolia (Paraná pine); Agathis spp. (kauri)

common_names: Alerce; Patagonian cypress; lahuán
heartwood: Reddish-brown to dark red-brown; old-growth wood often with very narrow, regular rings.
key_diagnostic: Reddish non-resin-canal softwood with very narrow regular growth rings and cedar scent. Typical shingles, roof tiles, furniture of old-growth origin.
lookalikes: Pilgerodendron uviferum; Sequoia sempervirens (redwood); Thuja plicata (western red cedar)

common_names: Guaitecas cypress; ciprés de las Guaitecas
heartwood: Yellowish to light reddish-brown.
key_diagnostic: Aromatic, fine-textured cypress-type softwood without resin canals; from Patagonia. Hand lens gives family level only.
lookalikes: Fitzroya cupressoides; Austrocedrus chilensis; Chamaecyparis spp.

common_names: Parlatore's podocarp; pino del cerro
heartwood: Uniform pale yellowish-brown.
key_diagnostic: Featureless, uniform yellowish softwood without resin canals and with indistinct rings (typical Podocarpus).
lookalikes: Other Podocarpus spp.; Prumnopitys spp.

population_scope: All species except D. nigra (App. I). D. cochinchinensis = #4; Mexican populations = #6.
common_names: Rosewoods; palisanders; blackwoods; hongmu (part)
deposits: red-brown to black gum in some pores
heartwood: Very variable: purple-brown, red-orange, chocolate, nearly black; often streaked.
odour: Many species fragrant (rose, spicy, sweet) when cut or sanded.
key_diagnostic: GENUS LEVEL: diffuse-porous, few medium/large pores, fine banded + aliform parenchyma, storied rays (ripple marks), dark often fragrant heartwood. Treat any wood matching this pattern as SUSPECT Dalbergia (CITES App II) until proven otherwise.
lookalikes: Machaerium spp. (pau ferro, Bolivian rosewood - NOT listed); Pterocarpus spp.; Millettia laurentii (wenge); Swartzia spp.; Diospyros spp. (ebony); Bobgunnia; Microberlinia (zebrawood)

scientific_name: Guibourtia demeusei, G. pellegriniana, G. tessmannii
population_scope: All populations of the three species
common_names: Bubinga; kevazingo (rotary veneer); African rosewood; essingang
heartwood: Pinkish-red to reddish-brown with darker purple or red veins; figured (pommele, waterfall).
odour: Unpleasant when wet/green, none when dry.
key_diagnostic: Pinkish-red, purple-veined heartwood; medium pores often gum-filled; aliform-confluent parenchyma; NO ripple marks (helps separate from Dalbergia and Pterocarpus). Three listed species cannot be separated from each other or from unlisted Guibourtia (e.g. G. ehie - ovangkol) by hand lens.
lookalikes: Guibourtia ehie (ovangkol/shedua - not listed); Guibourtia coleosperma (Rhodesian copalwood); Dalbergia spp.; Pterocarpus soyauxii

population_scope: All populations (also covered by the 2023 African Pterocarpus listing)
common_names: Kosso; African rosewood; vène; barwood; hongmu (part)
deposits: dark red gum in some pores
heartwood: Golden-red to purplish red-brown with darker streaks.
key_diagnostic: Red-purple 'rosewood' with semi-ring-porous tendency, fine wavy parenchyma bands and clear ripple marks. Top species in illegal West African hongmu log trade (round logs, squared beams). No annotation - all parts covered.
lookalikes: Pterocarpus tinctorius; Pterocarpus santalinus; Dalbergia spp.; Pterocarpus soyauxii (padauk)

common_names: Red sanders; red sandalwood; rakta chandana; zitan (part)
heartwood: Very dark blood-red to purplish-black; red pigment (santalin) stains water and fingers.
odour: None (despite the name it is NOT fragrant - unlike true sandalwood Santalum).
key_diagnostic: Extremely dense, very dark red, non-fragrant wood; parenchyma in fine wavy bands; ripple marks; red dye leaches into water/alcohol. Annotation #7: logs, chips, powder and extracts only.
lookalikes: Pterocarpus tinctorius (mukula); Pterocarpus erinaceus; Dalbergia cochinchinensis; Adenanthera pavonina; Caesalpinia sappan (sappanwood)

common_names: Mukula; African padauk (east/south); mulombe
heartwood: Bright red to deep red-brown, darkening with exposure.
key_diagnostic: Red Pterocarpus pattern (banded parenchyma, ripple marks). Shipments of red logs out of southern/eastern Africa to Asia should be treated as suspect mukula/red sanders.
lookalikes: Pterocarpus santalinus; Pterocarpus angolensis; Pterocarpus erinaceus

common_names: African padauk; muninga; mukwa; kiaat; barwood
heartwood: Orange-red (padauk) to golden-brown (kiaat/muninga).
key_diagnostic: Same genus pattern as above. Proposal at CoP20 to remove Central African P. soyauxii was REJECTED - still listed.
lookalikes: Dalbergia spp.; Baphia nitida (camwood); Guibourtia spp.

scientific_name: Swietenia macrophylla, S. humilis, S. mahagoni
annotation: S. macrophylla #6 (Neotropical populations); S. humilis #4; S. mahagoni #5
population_scope: S. macrophylla: Neotropics only (plantations in Asia/Fiji not covered)
common_names: Big-leaf mahogany; Honduras mahogany; genuine mahogany; caoba; Cuban mahogany; Pacific coast mahogany
deposits: dark red-brown gum and/or white deposits in some pores
heartwood: Light pinkish to deep reddish-brown, darkening; lustrous with ribbon figure.
key_diagnostic: Diffuse-porous reddish wood with medium pores (solitary + short radial multiples), white or dark gum deposits, distinct marginal parenchyma lines and frequent ripple marks.
lookalikes: Khaya spp. (African mahogany - usually no ripple marks, often no marginal lines); Carapa guianensis (andiroba); Cedrela spp.; Entandrophragma spp. (sapele, sipo); Toona spp.

common_names: Spanish cedar; cigar-box cedar; cedro; cedro rosado
deposits: dark red gum in some pores
heartwood: Light pinkish to reddish-brown; may exude resin/gum.
odour: Strong, characteristic spicy-cedar scent (cigar boxes) - key field feature.
key_diagnostic: Light, soft, aromatic reddish wood that is ring/semi-ring porous with marginal parenchyma - the scent plus ring porosity separates it from Swietenia.
lookalikes: Toona spp. (Asian/Australian red cedar - not listed); Swietenia spp.; Carapa spp.; Cedrela plantations outside the Neotropics (Africa) - not covered

common_names: African mahogany; acajou d'Afrique; khaya; lagos mahogany; mbawa
deposits: dark red-brown gum in some pores
heartwood: Pale pinkish-brown to reddish-brown; ribbon/stripe figure from interlocked grain.
key_diagnostic: Mahogany-type wood without ripple marks and usually with indistinct ring boundaries, interlocked grain. Hand lens: Khaya-group (vs Swietenia ripple marks + marginal lines).
lookalikes: Swietenia spp.; Entandrophragma spp. (sapele, sipo, tiama, kosipo - NOT listed); Lovoa trichilioides; Carapa procera

population_scope: Populations of Africa only (Asian merbau Intsia and Asian Afzelia xylocarpa NOT covered)
common_names: Doussié; afzelia; pod mahogany; chanfuta; lingue; mkora
deposits: YELLOW to whitish deposits in pores (characteristic)
heartwood: Light brown to reddish-/orange-brown, darkening.
key_diagnostic: Large, few pores with YELLOWISH-WHITE deposits + lozenge/confluent parenchyma + orange-brown heartwood. Proposal at CoP20 to remove Central African A. bipindensis was rejected - still listed.
lookalikes: Intsia bijuga / I. palembanica (merbau - not listed, also has yellow deposits); Afzelia xylocarpa (Asian, not covered); Pericopsis elata; Milicia excelsa (iroko - has white deposits)

scientific_name: Handroanthus spp., Roseodendron spp., Tabebuia spp.
common_names: Ipê; ipe; lapacho; Brazilian walnut; trumpet tree; guayacán; primavera (Roseodendron)
heartwood: Olive-brown to dark brown with greenish/yellowish cast (Handroanthus); Roseodendron & many Tabebuia much paler.
key_diagnostic: Very heavy olive-brown wood, small numerous pores with YELLOW deposits that turn red with alkali, storied structure. Common products: decking (HS 4409) - covered by #17.
lookalikes: Dipteryx spp. (cumaru - no yellow powder, vanilla scent); Tabebuia lighter species; Diplotropis/ sucupira; Manilkara (massaranduba - red, no ripple marks); Hymenaea (jatoba)

common_names: Cumaru; shihuahuaco; Brazilian teak; tonka bean tree; almendro (D. oleifera)
heartwood: Medium yellowish- to reddish-brown, sometimes purplish streaks; darkens.
key_diagnostic: Very heavy brown wood with storied structure and winged-aliform parenchyma; coumarin (vanilla) scent; NO yellow lapachol powder (separates from ipê).
lookalikes: Handroanthus (ipê); Hymenaea courbaril (jatoba); Pericopsis elata; Diplotropis purpurea

common_names: Pernambuco; pau-brasil; Brazilwood; bois de Pernambouc
heartwood: Bright orange to orange-red when fresh, darkening to deep red-brown; lustrous.
key_diagnostic: Very heavy, fine-textured orange-red wood (bow blanks!). CoP20 adopted new decisions on traceability of bows, blanks and stockpiles - scrutinise bow-maker consignments.
lookalikes: Caesalpinia/Biancaea sappan (sappanwood); Haematoxylum brasiletto; Manilkara bidentata (massaranduba - used for cheap bows); Handroanthus (ipê - 'pau ferro' bows); Pterocarpus spp.

common_names: Ramin; melawis; lanutan-bagyo
heartwood: Uniform pale straw to creamy white (no heartwood colour).
key_diagnostic: Featureless pale wood used for dowels/mouldings with distinct winged-aliform to confluent parenchyma under the lens. Annotation #4 covers finished products.
lookalikes: Alstonia (pulai); Dyera (jelutong); Fagus (beech); Tilia (basswood); Koompassia/ Paraserianthes

common_names: Agarwood; gaharu; oud; aloeswood; eaglewood; chen xiang; jinkoh
deposits: dark resin in tissues of agarwood
heartwood: Healthy wood: pale yellowish-white, very light, soft. Resinous agarwood: dark brown to black patches/streaks, heavy (may sink).
density: ~350-450 kg/m3 healthy; resinous agarwood much heavier
odour: Resin-impregnated wood: strong sweet, balsamic fragrance, especially when warmed/burned.
key_diagnostic: Light pale wood with scattered islands of INCLUDED PHLOEM, or dark resinous chips/ 'wood' with strong fragrance. Traded as chips, powder, oil, beads, carvings - #14 covers most.
lookalikes: Fake/impregnated agarwood (other woods soaked in oil/resin); Excoecaria agallocha; Gonystylus (also Thymelaeaceae)

common_names: Afrormosia; assamela; kokrodua; African teak
heartwood: Yellowish-brown when fresh, darkening to golden/olive-brown (teak-like), lustrous.
key_diagnostic: Teak-coloured wood that is diffuse porous with storied structure and aliform-confluent parenchyma (teak is semi-ring porous, oily, without ripple marks).
lookalikes: Tectona grandis (teak); Milicia excelsa (iroko); Afzelia spp.; Nauclea diderrichii (opepe)

common_names: Trebol; macacaúba (genus); Panama redwood (genus)
heartwood: Red to reddish-brown/ purplish with darker stripes.
key_diagnostic: Red striped rosewood-like wood with storied structure. Only P. parviflorum listed - other Platymiscium (macacaúba, P. pinnatum) are not.
lookalikes: Dalbergia spp.; Other Platymiscium spp. (not listed); Pterocarpus spp.

common_names: Madagascar ebony; ébène; hazomainty
heartwood: Jet black, sometimes with grey/brown streaks.
key_diagnostic: Jet black, very heavy fine-textured wood; small pores in short radial multiples; fine reticulate parenchyma lines. Origin is decisive (only Madagascar listed).
lookalikes: Diospyros crassiflora (Gabon ebony - not listed); Diospyros celebica (macassar); Dalbergia melanoxylon; Dyed/ blackened woods

common_names: Argentine lignum vitae; palo santo (Gran Chaco); verawood (trade); guaiac wood
heartwood: Olive-green to brown, darkening; oily.
odour: Pleasant, incense/rose-like (guaiac wood oil) - strong when sanded or burned.
key_diagnostic: Green-olive, oily, fragrant, very heavy wood with small solitary pores and very fine ripple marks. Do not confuse the trade name 'palo santo' with Bursera graveolens (not listed).
lookalikes: Guaiacum spp.; Bulnesia arborea (verawood - not listed); Bursera graveolens (palo santo sticks)

common_names: Lignum vitae; guayacán; gaïac
heartwood: Dark greenish-brown to almost black; very oily/ waxy.
key_diagnostic: Extremely heavy, oily, green-brown wood with tiny solitary pores and very fine ripple marks. Traded as bearings, mallets, carvings.
lookalikes: Bulnesia spp.; Handroanthus (ipê); Diospyros

population_scope: Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania
common_names: East African sandalwood; African sandalwood
heartwood: Yellowish to light brown, oily.
odour: Sandalwood-like fragrance, weaker than Santalum album.
key_diagnostic: Small fragrant yellowish logs/roots from East Africa with very fine texture. Smell + origin are key.
lookalikes: Santalum album (Indian sandalwood - not CITES); Santalum spicatum

common_names: African cherry; pygeum; red stinkwood
heartwood: Pinkish-brown to reddish-brown.
key_diagnostic: Usually encountered as dried bark chips/powder (prostate medicine) - bitter almond odour. Wood is a fine cherry-like hardwood.
lookalikes: Other Prunus spp.

common_names: Brazilian rosewood (oil); pau-rosa; bois de rose (oil)
heartwood: Yellowish-brown to brownish.
odour: Strong floral/ linalool (rose) scent - source of rosewood essential oil.
key_diagnostic: NOT a 'rosewood' timber in the Dalbergia sense; traded mostly as oil. Wood: fragrant yellowish-brown Lauraceae.
lookalikes: Other Aniba / Ocotea spp.

common_names: Gavilán; caribe
heartwood: Light brown to pinkish brown.
key_diagnostic: Rarely encountered in trade; walnut-like Juglandaceae wood.
lookalikes: Alfaroa spp.; Juglans spp.

scientific_name: Taxus chinensis, T. cuspidata, T. fuana, T. sumatrana, T. wallichiana (and their infraspecific taxa)
population_scope: All populations of the listed species
common_names: Asian yews; Chinese yew; Japanese yew; Himalayan yew
heartwood: Orange-red to purplish brown.
key_diagnostic: Dense orange-red softwood without resin canals, very narrow rings and thin white sapwood. Species not separable by wood - origin/DNA.
lookalikes: Taxus baccata (European yew - not listed); Taxus brevifolia (Pacific yew); Torreya spp.

common_names: Mulanje cedar
heartwood: Pale reddish- to pinkish-brown.
key_diagnostic: Aromatic reddish cypress-family softwood from Malawi; curios, planks. Origin key.
lookalikes: Widdringtonia nodiflora / W. cedarbergensis; Juniperus procera (African pencil cedar)

population_scope: Population of the Russian Federation (listed by Russia)
common_names: Korean pine; Korean cedar; hong song; kedr (RU)
heartwood: Light reddish-brown / pinkish.
key_diagnostic: Soft pine with resin canals and GRADUAL earlywood-latewood transition (white pine type) - separates it from Scots pine/larch with abrupt transition.
lookalikes: Pinus sibirica (Siberian pine - not listed); Pinus strobus; Pinus sylvestris (abrupt transition); Larix (abrupt transition, fewer canals)

population_scope: Population of the Russian Federation (listed by Russia)
common_names: Mongolian oak; Japanese oak (mizunara); Manchurian oak
heartwood: Light yellowish- to medium brown.
key_diagnostic: Typical white oak: ring porous, broad rays, tyloses in pores, flame-like latewood pore pattern. Cannot be separated from other white oaks by hand lens - origin (Russia) and documents are key.
lookalikes: Quercus robur / Q. petraea (European oak); Quercus alba (American white oak); Quercus crispula

population_scope: Population of the Russian Federation (listed by Russia)
common_names: Manchurian ash; tamo (figured); Japanese ash (yachidamo)
heartwood: Light greyish-brown to light brown.
key_diagnostic: Ring-porous ash: large earlywood pores, latewood pores with vasicentric/confluent parenchyma, fine rays. Separation from other ashes needs DNA/origin.
lookalikes: Fraxinus excelsior (European ash); Fraxinus americana (white ash); Fraxinus chinensis/ F. rhynchophylla; Castanea (chestnut)

common_names: Oleander podocarp; thitmin
heartwood: Uniform pale yellowish-brown.
key_diagnostic: Featureless Podocarpus wood; only Nepal-origin material is listed.
lookalikes: Other Podocarpus spp.; Nageia spp.

population_scope: Population of Nepal (listed by Nepal) - VERIFY current status on Species+
common_names: Spur-leaf tree; shui qing shu
heartwood: Light brown.
key_diagnostic: Vesselless angiosperm: no pores, but rays wider than any softwood. Very rare in trade.
lookalikes: Trochodendron aralioides (also vesselless); Drimys spp.

population_scope: Population of Nepal (listed by Nepal) - VERIFY current status on Species+
common_names: Champ (Nepal)
heartwood: Olive-greenish to yellowish-brown.
key_diagnostic: Fine, even Magnoliaceae wood with marginal parenchyma lines and greenish heartwood. Only Nepal origin listed.
lookalikes: Michelia/ Magnolia spp.; Liriodendron
